title: Final Next.js Engineering Assessment

questions.prompt: In the context of “Introduction to Next.js” and “Definition of Next.js”, Next.js is best described as
options: a programming language that replaces JavaScript.
a React framework that adds routing, rendering choices, and full-stack conventions.
a database engine for storing application records.
a CSS preprocessor that only compiles stylesheets.
questions.answer_key: a React framework that adds routing, rendering choices, and full-stack conventions.
questions.explanation: Next.js builds on React and provides application conventions and server capabilities; it does not replace JavaScript or serve as a database.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Next.js vs React vs Other Web Frameworks”, Which comparison is accurate for this part of the curriculum?
options: React is a UI library; Next.js is a framework that organizes a complete web application around React.
React and Next.js are both database products.
Next.js can only render static HTML and cannot support interactive UI.
A Vite-based React app and a Next.js app always have identical server features.
questions.answer_key: React is a UI library; Next.js is a framework that organizes a complete web application around React.
questions.explanation: React supplies the component model; Next.js supplies additional routing, rendering, and server-side application conventions.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Installing Development Tools”, Before diagnosing a setup failure, which evidence is most useful?
options: Delete the lockfile and dependencies immediately without recording the error.
Change unrelated framework versions until the error disappears.
Check Node.js and package-manager versions, the terminal error, package scripts, and the project’s installed Next.js version.
Assume every terminal failure is a browser cache problem.
questions.answer_key: Check Node.js and package-manager versions, the terminal error, package scripts, and the project’s installed Next.js version.
questions.explanation: Reproducible setup troubleshooting begins with versions and the actual error, not unrelated changes.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Understanding Package Scripts and Commands” and “Development commands”, For the Next.js 16 documentation snapshot used in this course, the minimum Node.js version documented by the official installation guide is
options: Node.js 14.0.
Node.js 16.0.
any Node.js version, because Next.js does not use a runtime.
Node.js 20.9.
questions.answer_key: Node.js 20.9.
questions.explanation: The official installation documentation checked for this course specifies Node.js 20.9 or later; verify the requirements for the version you install.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Understanding the Next.js Project Structure”, What is the primary purpose of a `layout.jsx` file?
options: To store environment secrets for all pages.
To define shared UI that wraps child routes and can persist across navigation.
To define an HTTP endpoint for every request method.
To replace all route pages with one global component.
questions.answer_key: To define shared UI that wraps child routes and can persist across navigation.
questions.explanation: Layouts provide shared route-segment UI and preserve structure across eligible child navigations.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Reusable Components and Folder Organization”, Where should database access and reusable domain rules generally live?
options: In clearly separated server/data-access modules rather than mixed into every page component.
In the public assets folder.
In the browser bundle with database credentials.
Only inside configuration comments.
questions.answer_key: In clearly separated server/data-access modules rather than mixed into every page component.
questions.explanation: Separating route files from trusted data access improves reuse and helps keep secrets out of client bundles.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Static Assets and Public Files” and “The public folder”, In the App Router, which file convention supplies the UI for a route?
options: A `page.jsx` file inside the route’s folder.
A `README.md` file beside the project.
A `package-lock.json` file inside `public/`.
An arbitrary component file anywhere in the repository with no route export.
questions.answer_key: A `page.jsx` file inside the route’s folder.
questions.explanation: The App Router uses reserved file conventions; `page.jsx` makes a route segment publicly accessible.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Catch-All and Optional Catch-All Routes”, For an internal navigation link in a page, which API is the usual declarative choice?
options: A hard-coded database connection string.
The `Image` component from `next/image`.
A Route Handler exported as a React component.
The `Link` component from `next/link`.
questions.answer_key: The `Link` component from `next/link`.
questions.explanation: `Link` is the standard component for navigation to internal routes; route handlers define HTTP endpoints instead.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Programmatic Navigation”, What should a detail route do when its identifier is invalid or the record does not exist?
options: Return a fake record to preserve the layout.
Validate the identifier and render an appropriate not-found response rather than pretending the record exists.
Expose a stack trace containing secrets.
Redirect every invalid route to an unrelated third-party URL.
questions.answer_key: Validate the identifier and render an appropriate not-found response rather than pretending the record exists.
questions.explanation: Missing or invalid resources should be handled intentionally, with useful user-facing behavior and no private diagnostics.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Navigation Performance” and “Client-side transitions”, What URL is matched by `app/products/[slug]/page.jsx`?
options: Only the literal URL `/products/[slug]`.
Every URL on the site, regardless of path.
A product-detail route such as `/products/blue-mug`, with `slug` containing `blue-mug`.
A JSON API endpoint automatically created at `/api/products`.
questions.answer_key: A product-detail route such as `/products/blue-mug`, with `slug` containing `blue-mug`.
questions.explanation: Bracketed folder names create dynamic URL segments; their values are available as route parameters.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Server and Client Component Boundaries”, When is the `use client` directive appropriate?
options: At the boundary of UI that needs state, event handlers, or browser-only APIs.
For every static heading, regardless of need.
To make server-only credentials safe to expose publicly.
To allow a Server Component to directly use browser storage during server render.
questions.answer_key: At the boundary of UI that needs state, event handlers, or browser-only APIs.
questions.explanation: Use Client Components for interactivity and browser APIs; the directive does not make secrets safe for the browser.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Context Providers in the App Router”, How can a page reduce unnecessary client JavaScript?
options: Mark the root of the application as a Client Component by default.
Move all database queries into the browser.
Duplicate every component to force hydration.
Keep data loading and static composition on the server and isolate interactive elements in smaller Client Components.
questions.answer_key: Keep data loading and static composition on the server and isolate interactive elements in smaller Client Components.
questions.explanation: Deliberate server/client boundaries reduce bundle cost and clarify where code executes.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Rendering Architecture Patterns” and “Server-first architecture”, In the App Router, which component type is the default?
options: A Client Component with every page marked `use client`.
A standalone Web Worker.
A Pages Router API endpoint.
A React Server Component.
questions.answer_key: A React Server Component.
questions.explanation: Server Components are the default in the App Router; the client boundary is introduced where browser interactivity is needed.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Responsive Web Design”, Which approach is a good starting point for responsive layout?
options: Set a fixed desktop width for every viewport.
Use color alone to convey every status.
Use flexible layouts and mobile-first styles, then add breakpoints when content needs them.
Hide all keyboard focus indicators to save space.
questions.answer_key: Use flexible layouts and mobile-first styles, then add breakpoints when content needs them.
questions.explanation: Responsive layouts adapt to available space; test real content, text scaling, and keyboard use at multiple sizes.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Animation and Interaction Styling”, What should a shared design system define?
options: Consistent tokens and component patterns for typography, spacing, states, and accessible controls.
A different arbitrary spacing value for each page.
Unreviewed global overrides for every component.
Only screenshots without component behavior or documentation.
questions.answer_key: Consistent tokens and component patterns for typography, spacing, states, and accessible controls.
questions.explanation: Design tokens and documented component APIs help keep UI behavior and appearance consistent.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Fetching Data from External APIs” and “REST API requests”, Where is a suitable place to fetch private application data when using the App Router?
options: Inside a publicly shipped bundle with credentials embedded.
In trusted server-side code such as a Server Component or server-only data-access module.
Inside the image alt text.
Only after sending database credentials from the browser.
questions.answer_key: In trusted server-side code such as a Server Component or server-only data-access module.
questions.explanation: Server-side data access can keep credentials out of the client bundle, but authorization and safe data shaping are still required.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Parallel Data Fetching”, Why should a `fetch` example check `response.ok` before parsing expected data?
options: Because `response.ok` automatically validates the JSON schema.
Because every request returns a successful status.
Because it makes a remote endpoint trustworthy without checking it.
An HTTP failure can still return a response object, so the code should handle non-success status explicitly.
questions.answer_key: An HTTP failure can still return a response object, so the code should handle non-success status explicitly.
questions.explanation: Check status and validate the received shape; HTTP success alone does not guarantee complete or trusted data.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Data Validation and Transformation”, How can independent data requests avoid an unnecessary request waterfall?
options: Always await every independent request one after the other.
Fetch data in a Client Component even when no browser interaction is needed.
Run independent operations concurrently, for example with `Promise.all`, and define partial-failure behavior where needed.
Ignore one request’s rejection without defining the UI behavior.
questions.answer_key: Run independent operations concurrently, for example with `Promise.all`, and define partial-failure behavior where needed.
questions.explanation: Parallel requests can reduce waiting time, while error handling still needs to match the page’s requirements.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Fetch Cache Options” and “Cache-related Fetch options”, Before caching data, what is the most important correctness question?
options: Whether caching makes tests unnecessary.
Whether private data can share one global cache key across users.
Whether the data may be shared, how fresh it must be, and which user/request dimensions affect the result.
Whether the same defaults apply to every Next.js release.
questions.answer_key: Whether the data may be shared, how fresh it must be, and which user/request dimensions affect the result.
questions.explanation: Cache behavior depends on the configured model and data sensitivity; user-specific results must not leak across cache boundaries.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Static Rendering and Prerendering”, What should happen when a mutation changes content that was cached?
options: Assume all clients refresh automatically in every situation.
Invalidate or revalidate the relevant route/data according to the chosen cache strategy.
Delete every unrelated database table.
Disable authorization until the cache expires.
questions.answer_key: Invalidate or revalidate the relevant route/data according to the chosen cache strategy.
questions.explanation: A cache strategy needs an explicit path or tag invalidation plan that matches which data changed.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Component-Level Loading States”, What belongs in a production error message?
options: A safe explanation and a recovery or retry path, while sensitive diagnostics stay in server logs.
Full stack traces and secret values.
An unconditional success message.
The raw body of every rejected upstream response.
questions.answer_key: A safe explanation and a recovery or retry path, while sensitive diagnostics stay in server logs.
questions.explanation: Production experiences should aid recovery without disclosing internals.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Redirects and Control Flow” and “Using redirect utilities”, What does an App Router `loading.jsx` convention provide?
options: A route-segment loading UI, commonly connected to a Suspense boundary.
A persistent database migration.
The answer key for an exam.
A security check that replaces route authorization.
questions.answer_key: A route-segment loading UI, commonly connected to a Suspense boundary.
questions.explanation: The loading convention supplies pending UI; it does not replace data validation or authorization.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Introduction to Forms in Next.js”, What does the `FormData` interface provide in a form submission?
options: Proof that the user is an administrator.
An automatic database transaction and authorization policy.
A signed and trusted replacement for the request body.
A way to read submitted form fields that still need type, format, and business-rule validation.
questions.answer_key: A way to read submitted form fields that still need type, format, and business-rule validation.
questions.explanation: FormData is a representation of submitted values, not a guarantee that the values or caller are valid.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Input Validation and Schema Validation”, After a successful mutation that changes cached content, what is a sensible next step?
options: Report success before persistence finishes.
Revalidate affected data/routes and return or redirect with an accurate result.
Assume every unrelated route must be invalidated.
Disable the permission check for the next request.
questions.answer_key: Revalidate affected data/routes and return or redirect with an accurate result.
questions.explanation: Mutation UX should reflect the actual operation and refresh the specific data that became stale.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Progressive Enhancement” and “Forms with minimal client JavaScript”, What should a Server Action do before mutating protected data?
options: Trust client-side button visibility as the only access check.
Accept every submitted field without validation.
Validate untrusted input and re-check authentication, authorization, and resource ownership on the server.
Return success before attempting the database operation.
questions.answer_key: Validate untrusted input and re-check authentication, authorization, and resource ownership on the server.
questions.explanation: Server Actions are reachable through request boundaries; they need server-side validation and authorization in the action itself.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Working with Request Data”, What is a key difference between direct server-side data fetching and a Route Handler?
options: A Server Component can often call trusted data functions directly, while a Route Handler exposes an HTTP endpoint.
A Route Handler is always required for every server-side database query.
A Route Handler is a stylesheet convention.
Server Components cannot access server-side data.
questions.answer_key: A Server Component can often call trusted data functions directly, while a Route Handler exposes an HTTP endpoint.
questions.explanation: Avoid unnecessary internal HTTP round trips when direct server-side data access fits the architecture.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “API Security”, How should an external webhook be processed?
options: Trust any JSON request with an event name.
Process duplicate deliveries as new payments every time.
Expose the signing secret in a public response.
Verify its signature, validate the event, and make processing idempotent for retries or duplicates.
questions.answer_key: Verify its signature, validate the event, and make processing idempotent for retries or duplicates.
questions.explanation: Webhook requests require sender verification, safe event handling, and duplicate-delivery protection.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Choosing Between Route Handlers and External Backends” and “When Next.js is sufficient for server functionality”, Which file convention defines an App Router HTTP endpoint?
options: A `layout.jsx` file that exports a React component.
A CSS module.
An environment file inside `public/`.
A `route.js` file in the route segment.
questions.answer_key: A `route.js` file in the route segment.
questions.explanation: Route Handlers use the `route.js`/`route.ts` convention and implement HTTP methods explicitly.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Authentication Libraries”, Which cookie options are important to consider for a session cookie?
options: Only a colorful CSS class.
A `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix for the session secret.
`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and an appropriate `SameSite` policy, with scope and lifetime set intentionally.
A very long-lived cookie with no revocation strategy.
questions.answer_key: `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and an appropriate `SameSite` policy, with scope and lifetime set intentionally.
questions.explanation: Cookie attributes reduce exposure and cross-site risks, but session lifecycle and server-side validation still matter.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Protecting Server Actions”, Where should privileged operations enforce permissions?
options: Inside every relevant server-side mutation or handler, not only in the page or layout UI.
Only in the navigation menu.
Only in a client-side variable.
Only in a one-time login redirect.
questions.answer_key: Inside every relevant server-side mutation or handler, not only in the page or layout UI.
questions.explanation: A protected page can be requested through other paths; the operation itself must enforce access.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Security Audits and Secure Defaults” and “Dependency vulnerability checks”, What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
options: Authentication checks styles and authorization checks image dimensions.
Authentication establishes who the caller is; authorization checks what that caller may do.
They are identical words for client-side routing.
Authorization means a user has a valid email address, regardless of permissions.
questions.answer_key: Authentication establishes who the caller is; authorization checks what that caller may do.
questions.explanation: Identity and permission are separate checks and both may be needed for a protected resource.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Open Graph Metadata”, What makes a useful page title and description?
options: Every page uses the same keyword-stuffed title.
The description promises content the page does not contain.
The title is generated only from a random number.
They are unique, accurate summaries that match the page’s visible content and purpose.
questions.answer_key: They are unique, accurate summaries that match the page’s visible content and purpose.
questions.explanation: Metadata should help users and crawlers understand the real page; accuracy is more useful than keyword stuffing.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Structured Data”, What should be checked after generating a sitemap or social preview?
options: Assume creating the file proves every URL is indexable.
Publish private dashboard pages in the public sitemap.
Verify canonical URLs, route coverage, image availability, and that previews match the intended page.
Omit descriptions and canonical details on every dynamic route.
questions.answer_key: Verify canonical URLs, route coverage, image availability, and that previews match the intended page.
questions.explanation: Sitemaps and social metadata need validation and should not expose private routes or misleading content.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Image Optimization with next/image” and “The Image component”, What should be supplied for an image with meaningful content?
options: An empty alt value for every image, including informative diagrams.
A database password in the image URL.
Useful alternative text, correct dimensions or sizing behavior, and an appropriate loading strategy.
A fixed oversized asset regardless of viewport.
questions.answer_key: Useful alternative text, correct dimensions or sizing behavior, and an appropriate loading strategy.
questions.explanation: Alternative text depends on purpose; dimensions and loading strategy help accessibility and performance.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Favicons and Application Icons”, How should a remote image host be enabled for the Next.js Image component?
options: Allow all remote hosts by default without considering risk.
Allow-list the required remote source patterns as narrowly as practical.
Move image credentials into client-visible source code.
Disable dimension handling on every image.
questions.answer_key: Allow-list the required remote source patterns as narrowly as practical.
questions.explanation: A narrow remotePatterns configuration controls which remote image sources the optimization layer will accept.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Understanding State in Next.js Applications”, How should a form or optimistic UI handle a failed server mutation?
options: Keep showing success even though the operation failed.
Award completion based on the click alone.
Ignore returned validation messages.
Show a truthful error and reconcile or roll back optimistic state so UI and server data agree.
questions.answer_key: Show a truthful error and reconcile or roll back optimistic state so UI and server data agree.
questions.explanation: Optimistic updates improve responsiveness but need a well-defined failure and reconciliation path.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Client-Side Data Synchronization” and “Fetching current data”, Where should transient interactive UI state such as an open/closed panel usually live?
options: In a Client Component using React state where the interaction occurs.
Inside a public environment variable.
Only in a server database even when it is purely temporary UI state.
In the alt text of the page logo.
questions.answer_key: In a Client Component using React state where the interaction occurs.
questions.explanation: React state is appropriate for transient UI state; authoritative user data and security rules belong on the server.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Real-Time UI Concepts”, When is a Context provider a reasonable choice?
options: For every single local boolean in every component.
To expose database credentials to the browser.
When state such as theme or session-related display data is needed by many descendants, with provider scope kept deliberate.
To bypass server-side authorization.
questions.answer_key: When state such as theme or session-related display data is needed by many descendants, with provider scope kept deliberate.
questions.explanation: Place providers where consumers need them and avoid making large application regions client-rendered without reason.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Advanced Dynamic Routing”, What should advanced route composition test?
options: Only whether the folder name exists.
Direct URL loading, browser back/forward behavior, refresh behavior, and the appropriate fallback UI.
Only a screenshot of the modal state.
No behavior outside client-side navigation.
questions.answer_key: Direct URL loading, browser back/forward behavior, refresh behavior, and the appropriate fallback UI.
questions.explanation: Routing composition has several navigation paths, all of which should behave predictably.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Advanced Navigation UX” and “Preserving state”, What do parallel routes support in the App Router?
options: Running SQL queries in parallel automatically.
Rendering multiple named route slots within a shared layout.
Replacing authentication checks with separate page folders.
Adding query parameters without changing the route tree.
questions.answer_key: Rendering multiple named route slots within a shared layout.
questions.explanation: Parallel routes compose separate route slots; they are a routing/UI architecture feature rather than a database concurrency primitive.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Understanding Request Processing”, What is an appropriate use of Proxy?
options: Selective request-time routing or lightweight request handling where supported by the deployment model.
A universal substitute for authorization inside every protected server action.
A persistent worker for long-running background jobs in every host.
A place to store secrets in browser code.
questions.answer_key: Selective request-time routing or lightweight request handling where supported by the deployment model.
questions.explanation: Proxy can shape some incoming requests but does not replace permission checks in the final protected operation.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Headers and Cookies APIs”, What should guide the use of framework configuration options?
options: Assume every option works across all releases and hosts.
Copy experimental settings without documenting them.
Disable tests to avoid configuration errors.
Check the version-matched official reference and verify the setting in development and production builds.
questions.answer_key: Check the version-matched official reference and verify the setting in development and production builds.
questions.explanation: Framework configuration and platform support are version- and host-dependent.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Introduction to Testing Next.js Applications” and “Why applications need automated tests”, What should a unit test focus on?
options: The full deployed system exclusively.
Whether a button matches a screenshot only.
An unrepeatable production database modification.
A small unit of logic with controlled inputs and clear expected results.
questions.answer_key: A small unit of logic with controlled inputs and clear expected results.
questions.explanation: Unit tests target small units; integration and end-to-end tests are needed for broader boundaries and user journeys.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Testing Server Actions”, Which tests are especially useful for important user journeys?
options: Only checking that files exist.
Only unit-testing strings and assuming the whole application works.
End-to-end tests that exercise routing and interactions in a browser-like environment.
Running no tests when a route is changed.
questions.answer_key: End-to-end tests that exercise routing and interactions in a browser-like environment.
questions.explanation: End-to-end tests help verify behavior across routes, server boundaries, and client interactions.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Testing in Continuous Integration”, What should a meaningful regression test do?
options: Reproduce the previously failing case and assert the behavior that should remain fixed.
Repeat a vague manual click without an expected result.
Delete the failing test after the fix.
Check only that the code compiles even when runtime behavior was wrong.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the previously failing case and assert the behavior that should remain fixed.
questions.explanation: A stable regression test captures the failure mode and expected behavior so later changes do not silently reintroduce it.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Rendering Performance” and “Choosing static or dynamic rendering”, What is the first step when optimizing a slow page?
options: Rewrite every component without collecting evidence.
Measure a baseline and identify the bottleneck before choosing a fix.
Add more dependencies before understanding the bottleneck.
Assume all slowness comes from CSS.
questions.answer_key: Measure a baseline and identify the bottleneck before choosing a fix.
questions.explanation: Optimization should be evidence-driven: measure, identify, change, and measure again.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Measuring Real-World Performance”, How can a page reduce unnecessary client JavaScript?
options: Mark all modules as client-only regardless of use.
Import every feature on the first render.
Move secrets to the client to avoid server code.
Prefer Server Components for non-interactive composition and lazy-load genuinely optional client code.
questions.answer_key: Prefer Server Components for non-interactive composition and lazy-load genuinely optional client code.
questions.explanation: Server-first composition and careful splitting can reduce the browser bundle and improve startup work.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Accessible Navigation”, What is a robust way to test an interactive component?
options: Test only with a mouse.
Remove focus styling on hover.
Test keyboard and pointer use, visible focus, understandable state changes, and reduced-motion preferences where relevant.
Use animation as the only way to communicate a status.
questions.answer_key: Test keyboard and pointer use, visible focus, understandable state changes, and reduced-motion preferences where relevant.
questions.explanation: Accessibility checks should cover real interaction paths and should not rely only on visual color or motion.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Internationalized Routing” and “Locale-based routes”, What makes a form control accessible to a screen reader and other users?
options: A placeholder alone for every required field.
A color difference with no other signal.
Semantic markup and a programmatically associated accessible name, such as a label linked to the input.
A clickable `div` with no keyboard interaction.
questions.answer_key: Semantic markup and a programmatically associated accessible name, such as a label linked to the input.
questions.explanation: Labels, semantics, focus visibility, keyboard behavior, and understandable errors are important parts of accessible UI.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Preparing a Next.js Application for Production”, Where should production API keys and database credentials live?
options: In source control as examples with real values.
In the deployment environment or a secret manager, accessible only to the server-side code that requires them.
In `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables when they are private.
Inside an image URL included in the public page.
questions.answer_key: In the deployment environment or a secret manager, accessible only to the server-side code that requires them.
questions.explanation: Public-prefixed variables can reach the browser; production secrets should remain server-only.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Deployment with Containers”, What should be checked after deployment?
options: Only the landing page screenshot.
Only whether deployment returned a success notification.
No logs or monitoring because the build passed.
Runtime logs, health and key user flows, environment configuration, errors, and a rollback/recovery path.
questions.answer_key: Runtime logs, health and key user flows, environment configuration, errors, and a rollback/recovery path.
questions.explanation: A successful build alone does not validate production configuration, integrations, or user workflows.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Continuous Integration and Deployment” and “Automated build pipelines”, Which command commonly creates an optimized Next.js production build?
options: `npm run build`, if the project defines the standard build script.
`npm run start` before building, in every project.
`rm -rf .git`.
`python manage.py migrate`, regardless of the stack.
questions.answer_key: `npm run build`, if the project defines the standard build script.
questions.explanation: Inspect package.json for the project scripts; the standard build script typically runs `next build`.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Pages Router Page Components”, How should a Pages Router to App Router migration be approached?
options: Rename every folder at once without testing.
Delete route tests because the folder structure is different.
Migrate incrementally while preserving URLs and behavior and adding regression tests.
Mix data-fetching APIs without checking where they are supported.
questions.answer_key: Migrate incrementally while preserving URLs and behavior and adding regression tests.
questions.explanation: A staged migration with route parity checks reduces risk and makes failures easier to isolate.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “API Routes in the Pages Router”, Which rule helps maintain a legacy codebase?
options: Apply App Router-only APIs in every legacy page automatically.
Keep legacy conventions explicit and check each API against the version and router that use it.
Assume old caching and runtime behavior remain unchanged forever.
Ignore warnings and migration notes.
questions.answer_key: Keep legacy conventions explicit and check each API against the version and router that use it.
questions.explanation: Legacy maintenance depends on identifying router-specific behavior and verifying it against the installed version.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Migrating Layouts and Components” and “Moving shared UI into layouts”, Which statement best describes the Pages Router?
options: A CSS-only feature.
A supported routing system used by existing projects, with pages under `pages/` and its own data-fetching conventions.
The same filesystem convention as the App Router in every detail.
A feature removed from all Next.js versions.
questions.answer_key: A supported routing system used by existing projects, with pages under `pages/` and its own data-fetching conventions.
questions.explanation: The Pages Router remains relevant for maintenance, but it uses its own conventions distinct from the App Router.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Separating Business Logic”, Why centralize data access behind server-only functions?
options: It gives the application a clear place for query logic, data shaping, and permission-aware access.
It makes authorization unnecessary.
It prevents all database failures automatically.
It requires all code to run in the browser.
questions.answer_key: It gives the application a clear place for query logic, data shaping, and permission-aware access.
questions.explanation: Data-access modules centralize responsibilities but must still validate callers, handle errors, and limit returned fields.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Documentation and Maintainability”, What should a technical design record?
options: Only the final screenshot.
Secrets and passwords to simplify setup.
Key decisions, trade-offs, data boundaries, test strategy, operating assumptions, and how to verify the design.
A list of features with no explanation of data flow or failure behavior.
questions.answer_key: Key decisions, trade-offs, data boundaries, test strategy, operating assumptions, and how to verify the design.
questions.explanation: Professional workflows preserve the reasoning needed to review, operate, and change a system safely.

questions.prompt: In the context of “Understanding Common Setup Errors” and “Node.js version mismatches”, What is a strong first step when debugging a framework error?
options: Change several unrelated files at once.
Hide the error with a success banner.
Assume the same cause for every hydration warning.
Create a minimal reproducible case and record the full error and runtime/framework versions.
questions.answer_key: Create a minimal reproducible case and record the full error and runtime/framework versions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproduction, version check, and complete error context help separate application bugs from environment issues.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Data Fetching and Cache Bugs”, What is a hydration mismatch?
options: A failed database migration by definition.
A difference between the server-rendered output and the initial client-rendered output for the same UI.
A missing CSS file in every case.
A normal state that never requires investigation.
questions.answer_key: A difference between the server-rendered output and the initial client-rendered output for the same UI.
